### [Gemini Live audio](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Sep/15/gemini-live/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-09-15

Google released Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking speech-to-speech models, which support interactive voice conversations via a WebSockets API.

- Google launched two speech-to-speech models: Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking.
- The API uses a bidirectional WebSocket endpoint at wss://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/ws/google.ai.generativelanguage.v1alpha.GenerativeService.BidiGenerateContent.
- Browser implementations use the Web Audio API AudioContext for audio capture, playback, and handling user interruptions.
- A custom web UI was built using GPT-6 Astra Extra High to demonstrate model selection, voice presets, and system prompts.

**Why it matters:** Developers can now build real-time, interruptible voice-to-voice web applications directly through a Google WebSocket API using standard browser web audio interfaces.

### [The contagion of fear](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Sep/14/the-contagion-of-fear/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-09-14

Bryan Cantrill criticizes AI researchers for making speculative, unverified claims about existential risks like bioweapons and infrastructure hacking, warning experts against abusing public trust through fearmongering.

- Ex-Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon cited AI risks including hacking critical infrastructure and extinction-level bioweapons without detailed elaboration or domain expertise in those fields.
- Bryan Cantrill argues that catastrophic AI scenarios rely on hand-wavy extrapolations rather than concrete evidence from biologists or bioweapon experts.
- Cantrill emphasizes that domain experts hold implicit public trust and must remain circumspect when raising alarms regarding complex technical capabilities.

**Why it matters:** Sensationalized claims by AI insiders risk misleading the public and policy discussions through fear rather than grounded technical and domain-specific evidence.
